comparator.name: Earth System Sciences (formerly Soil, Water, Atmosphere)
comparator.academicYear: Current 2026–2027 curriculum and published cohort-2025 course scheme, checked 2026-09-28
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme is the renamed successor to Soil, Water, Atmosphere and totals 180 EC. The 2026–2027 handbook specifies 117 EC of compulsory credited courses, a 3-EC mathematics or statistics choice, 18 EC of restricted advanced options, a 12-EC thesis and 30 EC of free electives. The comparison selects Mathematics Applied: Introduction and the first three 6-EC restricted options in official order—Hydrogeology, Programming in Python and Sedimentary Geology—because no named route or broader substantive preference distinguishes the options. Required non-credit safety modules and the personal-development pathway are acknowledged here but are not encoded as credit-bearing components.

core: Earth-system interactions among soil, water, atmosphere and the biosphere
Physics, chemistry, mathematics, statistics, modelling and field measurement
Climate, weather and global environmental change
adjacent: Soils, geology, landscapes and sustainable land use
Hydrology, groundwater, water quality and river systems
Atmospheric processes, meteorology and climate dynamics
Geo-information, environmental data and computational modelling
Flood, drought, hazards, adaptation and disaster resilience
Ecology and biosphere interactions within Earth systems
questions: How can soil and water systems be understood and managed under floods, drought and land-use change?
How do atmospheric and climate processes interact with ecosystems and landscapes?
How can field measurement, spatial evidence and models reveal changes across the Earth system?

alternatives.label: Earth systems, climate & environmental evidence
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines the strongest available UCR sequence in Earth science, climate, soils, water, biogeochemistry, observation, quantitative methods and environmental research.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to Earth System Sciences: a physical and environmental programme linking Earth processes, climate, soils and water with quantitative evidence, geospatial observation and applied research.
progression: Sustainability, geology, programming and mathematics precede Earth-system tools, hazards, climate, observation, soils, water, numerical methods, biogeochemistry, data analysis and advanced environmental applications. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; six 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Climate, atmosphere & geospatial data
alternatives.labelReason: This pathway gives greater weight to climate processes, quantitative modelling, algorithms, Earth observation, machine learning and image-based spatial evidence.
alternatives.concept: A climate and atmosphere direction organised around Earth observation, quantitative modelling, computational analysis and geospatial evidence for environmental change and hazards.
progression: Earth science, programming and mathematical foundations precede Earth-system tools, linear algebra, numerical methods, observation, soils, machine learning, algorithms, computer vision and advanced environmental analysis. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; six 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes climate observation and computational spatial analysis the organising priority. Relative to the closest programme it replaces ecology, biodiversity, probability and remediation with linear algebra, algorithms, computer vision and nature-based adaptation; the pair differs by four courses and 30 EC in each direction.

alternatives.label: Soil, water, ecosystems & resilience
alternatives.labelReason: This pathway centres soils, aquifers, water, ecology, conservation, landscape processes and resilience while retaining Earth-system, climate and research foundations.
alternatives.concept: A soil-and-water direction connecting geology and hydrology with ecosystems, conservation, nature-based solutions, climate adaptation and the social dimensions of environmental resilience.
progression: Earth science, sustainability, ecology and life-science foundations precede conservation, climate, soils, aquifers, water systems, ecosystems, remediation, marine ecology, environmental justice and advanced research. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes soil, water, ecology and resilience the organising priority. It adds conservation, evolution, biodiversity, marine ecology, life science and environmental justice; it differs from each earlier alternative by at least five courses and 37.5 EC in each direction.

trace: Sustainability Essentials I supplies physical, mathematical and systems foundations for studying linked environmental change.
Dynamic Earth directly examines structural geology, Earth history and environmental geology.
Introduction to Programming develops Python-based computational problem solving for environmental data and models.
Sustainability Essentials II develops integrated systems analysis for environmental and climate questions.
Mathematical Methods develops calculus, linear algebra and differential-equation techniques used in Earth-system analysis.
Natural Hazards, Risks & Adaptations applies geoscience to disasters, environmental change and adaptation.
Earth System Science Tools uses tracers, proxies and greenhouse-gas pathways to analyse Earth-system change.
Climate Change directly studies anthropogenic climate change, ocean acidification and climate adaptation.
Introduction to Biodiversity establishes biological diversity within the biosphere component of Earth systems.
Introduction to Data Science develops cleaning, visualisation and analysis of spatial and other datasets.
Probability & Statistics develops probability, distributions and parameter estimation for environmental evidence.
Earth Observation directly uses satellite, drone and geospatial evidence to analyse environmental change.
Soils & Aquifers directly studies soil formation, aquifer mapping and freshwater-resource assessment.
Living with Water examines flood protection, freshwater management, land subsidence and ecological consequences.
Computational & Numerical Methods develops numerical modelling, root finding and differential-equation methods.
Environmental Biogeochemistry uses geochemical modelling to analyse waters, minerals and element cycles.
Research in a Sustainable Delta provides applied environmental research with an external partner.
R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation applies environmental chemistry to contamination, resources and remediation.
Machine Learning develops statistical learning methods for complex environmental and spatial datasets.
Earth’s Resources develops advanced geoscience around geothermal energy, subsurface storage and resource use.
Governance of Sustainability examines institutions and interests shaping climate adaptation and environmental action.
Renewable System Design develops advanced assessment and design of lower-carbon energy systems.
Ecosystems Uncovered directly examines ecological processes and interactions between organisms and environmental conditions.
Linear Algebra supplies vector and matrix methods used in spatial modelling and data science.
Building with Nature examines ecosystem-based design, land reclamation and flood protection.
Algorithms & Data Structures develops efficient computational methods for large and complex datasets.
Image Processing & Computer Vision develops methods directly relevant to satellite and environmental imagery.
Conservation Biology examines biodiversity loss and governance responses to sustainability challenges.
The Science of Evolution develops organism–environment reasoning relevant to changing ecosystems.
Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine supplies cellular and organismal foundations for biosphere processes.
Marine Biology examines estuaries, coasts and marine ecosystems within linked water–climate systems.
Social Movements & Environmental Justice develops the societal and justice dimensions of environmental resilience.

notes.text: WUR provides a prescribed specialist sequence in physics, chemistry, soil science, hydrology, meteorology, field measurement and advanced Earth-system options. UCR can combine substantial Earth science, climate, soils, water, ecology, observation and quantitative analysis, but it does not offer the same depth in atmospheric physics, meteorology, hydrology or field-based geoscience.

selection.assessment: The closest programme covers Earth systems, climate, soils, water, quantitative evidence and environmental research. Climate/atmosphere/geospatial data and soil/water/ecosystem resilience form two further independently evidenced, coherent and pairwise-distinct directions. All three are mechanically feasible; production stops at the maximum.
